summary: Walter Emile van Wijk specialized in Indology and history/archaeology, earning a doctorate in chemistry at Leiden University (~1916–1920). He served as PD at Leiden (1924, 1954) and directed Museon (1933–1938) and the Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris (1938–1953).

Walter Eugene Clark was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard, Berlin under Richard Pischel, and Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He taught at the University of Chicago (1908–1927) and Harvard (1927–1950).

Walter Ewer worked in the fields of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Fort William College (~1802–1804), served in the Bengal Civil Service (1803–1840), and became a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1840.

Walter Friedländer worked in history/archaeology and Indology, earning a Ph.D. under Albrecht Weber at Berlin. He held positions at the German Historical Institute in Rome, the University of Freiburg, the Art Institute of Chicago, and New York University.

Walter Kaufmann was an Indologist and ethnomusicologist who studied under Franz Schreker, Curt Sachs, Gustav Becking, and Paul Nettl. He headed All India Radio's classical music department (~1937–1946) and became Professor of Ethnomusicology at Indiana University Bloomington (1957–1977).

Walter Liebenthal studied Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology at several German universities under Otto Strauss, Johannes Nobel, and Max Walleser. He held posts at the Harvard-Yenching Institute, Peking University, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Tübingen.

Walter M. Spink was a scholar of history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Amherst College and Harvard University (PhD). He taught at Brandeis University (1956–1961) and served as a professor at the University of Michigan (~1961–2000).

Walter Neisser worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick.
Walter Nowick, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the Juilliard School and under Zuigan Goto. He taught at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.

Walter Petersen specialized in linguistics and Indology, completing a Ph.D. at Yale University (~1905–1908). He held posts at Bethany College (1908), the University of Florida (~1927–1929), and the University of Chicago (1930).

Walter Porzig, a linguist and Indologist, studied under Ernst Windisch, Ferdinand Sommer, Wilhelm Streitberg, and Friedrich Karl Slotty. He held professorships at the universities of Bern (1925), Jena (1935), Strasbourg (1941–1945), and Mainz (1951).

Walter Ruben, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied under Heinrich Lüders, Sten Konow, and Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Bonn, Frankfurt, Ankara University (1935–1948), the University of Chile (1948–1950), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1950–1965).

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics, studying at Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of London, where he served as Professor of Chinese (1947–1960).

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and served as Director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2019).
Walter Sutton Page specialized in Indology and linguistics. He served as Reader of Bengali at the University of Oxford and at SOAS University of London (~1921–1938).
Walter William Skeat was a linguist who was educated at King's College School, Highgate School, and Christ's College, Cambridge. He held a post at the University of Cambridge from ~1878 to 1912.

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University, the University of Oxford, and the University of Rennes, and was a disciple of Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).
Walther Eidlitz, active in Indology and religious studies, studied building engineering at TU Wien and studied under guru Swami Sadananda (~1939–1957).

Walther Heissig specialized in Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, earning degrees at Vienna, Göttingen, and Bonn. He taught at Fu Jen Catholic University and Peking University, later becoming Professor and Central Asian seminar Chair at Bonn.

Walther Marcus was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Giessen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Heidelberg University, where he earned his Ph.D. under Christian Bartholomae (~1912–1914).
